question: How does GPT-2-small mechanistically implement indirect object identification (IOI)?
hypothesis: GPT-2-small implements IOI through an attention-head circuit that, at the END position, attends from the prediction site to the indirect-object name token and copies its embedding into the residual stream, raising its logit above competing name candidates. The circuit likely involves earlier-layer components that identify the duplicated subject name and write a signal that biases later attention toward the non-duplicated (indirect-object) name. Specific layer and head identities, and the number of components involved, are unknown a priori and should be discovered by activation patching from corrupted runs.

behavior.description: Given an IOI prompt of the form 'When [A] and [B] went to the [place], [B] gave a [object] to', the model assigns higher logit to the indirect-object name (A) than to the subject name (B) at the final-token prediction position. Holds across both ABBA and BABA template orderings.

dataset.notes: IOI prompts in the Wang-et-al-2022 style. Each sample is generated from a sentence template such as 'When {A} and {B} went to the {place}, {B} gave a {object} to' (BABA order) or 'When {A} and {B} went to the {place}, {A} gave a {object} to' (ABBA order). Names are drawn from a closed list of common single-token first names that tokenize to a single GPT-2 BPE token with a leading space (e.g. ' John', ' Mary', ' Tom', ' Sarah', ' James', ' Kate', ' Robert', ' Lisa'). Places and objects are drawn from a closed single-token list. Both A and B must tokenize to a single token. The dataset is balanced 50/50 across ABBA and BABA orderings. A 100-sample heldout split is reserved for validation; dev/heldout splits use disjoint name pairs. The 'IO' token is the non-repeated name; the 'S' token is the repeated name. Length is held constant within an order group so positions align across clean and corrupted runs.

contrast.positive_template: When {A} and {B} went to the {place}, {B} gave a {object} to  -> {A}
contrast.negative_template: When {A} and {C} went to the {place}, {B} gave a {object} to  -> {A}

metadata.corruption_scheme: ABC: replace one of the two repeated names in the clean prompt with a third novel name C, leaving the END-position context unchanged but breaking the duplicate-name structure. This is the standard IOI activation-patching corruption from Wang et al. 2022.
metadata.tokenization_constraint: A, B, and C must all tokenize to a single GPT-2 BPE token with a leading space
metadata.length_constraint: clean and corrupted prompts must tokenize to identical length so that position indices align
metadata.balance_constraint: ABBA and BABA orderings split 50/50 in both clean and corrupted batches

stages.notes: Confirm GPT-2-small has a strong IOI behavioral signal. Measure accuracy (logit(IO) > logit(S) at the final position) and mean logit_diff = logit(IO) - logit(S) across all 500 dev samples. Abort if accuracy < 0.9. logit_diff requires SCALAR target_logits / foil_logits (one float per example), NOT full vocab arrays — extract logits[last_position, IO_token_id] and logits[last_position, S_token_id] only.

Two passes:

(1) Per-head sweep to RANK heads. Run autointerp.tools.head_patching.head_patch_sweep across all 144 (layer, head) pairs at the END position; this returns a [n_layers, n_heads] recovery matrix where each entry is the recovery from patching THAT HEAD ALONE. Use this matrix to identify the top-K heads (typically K=3 for IOI on GPT-2-small).

(2) JOINT recovery to FEED the criterion. After identifying the top-K via (1), compute the JOINT recovery — patching ALL K heads simultaneously in ONE forward pass:

```python
from autointerp.tools.head_patching import HeadPatch, cache_head_z, run_with_head_patches, logit_diff
clean_z = cache_head_z(handle, clean_prompts, layers=[L for (L,H) in top_K])
patches = [HeadPatch(layer=L, head=H, source=clean_z[L][:,:,H,:]) for (L,H) in top_K]
patched_logits = run_with_head_patches(handle, corrupt_prompts, patches, return_logits_at=-1)
joint_lD = logit_diff(patched_logits, IO_token_ids, S_token_ids).mean().item()
recovery = (joint_lD - corrupt_lD) / (clean_lD - corrupt_lD)  # SCALAR
```

Commit `recovery` (the JOINT scalar) as patch_effect_recovery's `patched_metric`. The criterion's `localization-recovery` threshold (0.85) is calibrated for the joint top-K, NOT per-head max from the sweep matrix. Do NOT commit head_patch_sweep['recovery'].max() — that is the per-head reading and will fail the criterion even when the circuit is correct.

Extract contrastive directions (IO vs S) from the residual stream at candidate layers identified in localization. Mean-ablate the top candidate heads from localization individually and measure ablation_drop on logit_diff. Confirm which heads cause large drops on the heldout-style patterns from your own measurements, not from priors. ablation_drop expects (baseline_metric, ablated_metric) scalars.

Path patching from candidate sender heads to the unembed (logit output) to confirm direct information flow. Build a candidate IOI circuit C from the heads and edges that survived your measurements. Measure circuit faithfulness by mean-ablating the COMPLEMENT of C (every head not in C) and running circuit-only forward passes:

```python
faithfulness = (circuit_only_logit_diff - corrupted_logit_diff) / (clean_logit_diff - corrupted_logit_diff)
```

faithfulness's required inputs are SCALARS: (circuit_metric, full_model_metric, corrupted_metric).

Evaluate the final candidate circuit on the 100-sample HELDOUT split (disjoint name pairs from dev). Report faithfulness (same formula as intervention stage, but on heldout). For minimality: sweep single-component removals from C, computing faithfulness with each component removed, and confirm each component contributes a non-trivial faithfulness drop:

```python
minimality = min(faithfulness_full - faithfulness_minus_one[i] for i in components)
```

minimality's required inputs are (full_circuit_faithfulness: float, removed_faithfulness: list[float] of length n_components). Use mean ablation as the ablation baseline.

success_criteria.description: GPT-2-small correctly prefers IO over S (logit_diff > 0) on at least 95% of dev samples

Patching the top-K attention heads JOINTLY into the corrupted run (all K heads' z-activations replaced from clean simultaneously in ONE forward pass via run_with_head_patches) recovers at least 0.85 of the clean-corrupt logit_diff gap on dev. This is the JOINT recovery scalar, NOT per-head max from head_patch_sweep. K is typically 3 for IOI on GPT-2-small. See localization stage notes for the exact code recipe.

Candidate IOI circuit (the K heads from localization) achieves faithfulness >= 0.85 on the heldout split. Faithfulness is computed by mean-ablating the COMPLEMENT of the circuit (all heads NOT in C) and measuring (circuit_only - corrupt) / (clean - corrupt) on heldout pairs. Heldout uses disjoint names from dev.

Every head in the final circuit causes a faithfulness drop >= 0.05 when removed (minimality). This is min(faithfulness_full - faithfulness_minus_one[i]) where component i is removed and the rest stay; the minimum across components must satisfy the threshold (i.e. the WEAKEST component is still load-bearing).

abort_if: Stage 1 accuracy < 0.9 — GPT-2-small should be near-ceiling on IOI; below this indicates a dataset or tokenization bug, not a real behavioral failure
Clean-corrupt logit_diff gap < 2.0 nats — contrastive signal too weak for meaningful patching
risks: Single-token name constraint shrinks the usable name pool; dev/heldout name disjointness must still hold or the heldout faithfulness number is contaminated
ABC corruption can leak into positions other than the swapped name; verify length-matching and position alignment before patching
Mean-ablation baseline can produce OOD activations at ablated heads; resampling ablation is a useful robustness check if faithfulness numbers look implausibly high or low
Patch_effect_recovery is sensitive to the choice of metric (logit_diff vs probability vs KL); fix the metric (logit_diff(IO,S)) at the start of localization and keep it consistent through validation
